markdown_report:
The best next step is a controlled recent-context replacement probe for each category’s single HSTU. At 10% research progress, improving diagnostic specificity is more feasible than introducing an unverified architectural change.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) User feedback favors recent, specific connections. It motivates testing recent-context sensitivity but does not establish that stronger recency weighting improves HR@10. (2) Existing deletions change evidence and sequence geometry together. Holding occupied positions fixed can reduce this ambiguity. (3) Removing the last item also changes the readout anchor. Preserve that item when investigating preceding context.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [HSTU](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152) combines attention biases and multiplicative gating. Input perturbations remain applicable without assuming which mechanisms the supplied implementation exposes. (2) [Activation-patching guidance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042) shows that corruption and output metrics affect localization. Use matched controls and report margins alongside ranks. (3) [Negative-sampling research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) motivates candidate controls. Shared candidates isolate paired changes without establishing full-catalog validity.

These insights define three directions: controlled context interventions, internal mechanism localization, and prospective validation of diagnostic predictions. A common framework separates **evidence changed**, **geometry preserved**, and **inference supported**:

| Probe | Evidence/geometry | Supported interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Existing deletion | Removed/changed | Joint content–position sensitivity |
| Proposed replacement | Substituted/preserved inputs | Corruption-specific content sensitivity |
| Internal patching | Activation restored/controlled | Component-specific recovery |

Three atomic ideas merit consideration. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Matched recent-versus-random replacement | 6/8/3 | Distinct control pairing; reusable; simple adapter change | Established perturbation method; uncertain predictive validity; replacement matching needs care |
| Final-position gate patching | 7/7/7 | HSTU mechanism focus; useful localization; bounded intervention | Established patching; corruption-dependent; requires verified internal hooks |
| Jointly learned recency bias | 4/7/4 | Minimal hypothesis; direct training test; one network | Familiar mechanism; may suppress useful older interests; predictor serialization must change |

**Selected algorithm.** Reserve the last training interaction as target; retain its preceding item as the observed anchor. For each eligible user, score intact history against 99 fixed unseen negatives. Replace equal numbers of recent and randomly selected preceding items using training-only, frequency-matched substitutes. Couple substitute draws across conditions; preserve occupied positions, lengths, masks, timestamps, and the anchor. Repeat several fixed corruption draws.

Report recent-minus-random changes in target rank, HR@10, and target-versus-highest-negative margin, with user-level paired bootstrap intervals. These are in-sample sensitivity measurements, not intent or generalization estimates.

Retain `DiagnosisProbe`, metric definitions, interpreter, and ModelView interfaces. Read features at the greatest nonzero index. Keep four category models, routing, seeds, training limits, and host evaluation unchanged; judge any subsequent training hypothesis solely by host macro validation HR@10.

idea.description: Add paired, frequency-matched recent-versus-random context replacement probes to the existing family-aware HSTU diagnostic adapter. Each category continues to use exactly one independently trained model.
idea.motivation: Current deletion probes conflate content loss with changes in sequence geometry. User feedback suggests examining recent specific context, but a controlled diagnostic is needed before increasing recency weighting.
idea.implementation_notes: Use training histories and training-only item frequencies. Reserve each eligible user's final training item as target, retaining the final observed context item unchanged. Select equal-size recent and random subsets from preceding occupied positions; allow their overlap and report it. Sample substitutes from predeclared frequency bins, excluding padding, target, and original history; reuse the substitute list across conditions. Preserve sequence length, occupied positions, anchor, and any supplied timestamps. Preserve RNG states and model mode. Return metrics and explicit definitions through DiagnosisProbe.run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and retain diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Use existing ModelView methods and the greatest nonzero position for readout. No checkpoint or predictor architecture changes are required for this diagnostic-only proposal. Host validation remains the selection criterion; diagnostic scores must not be substituted for it.
idea.pseudocode:
save RNG states and model mode
set the actual view.model to evaluation mode
for each eligible training user:
    target = history[-1]
    context = left_pad(truncate(history[:-1]))
    anchor = greatest_nonzero_index(context)
    candidates = fixed [target + 99 unique unseen negatives]
    intact_scores = score(context, candidates, readout=anchor)
    for each predeclared corruption draw:
        recent_positions = last k occupied positions before anchor
        random_positions = sample k occupied positions before anchor
        substitutes = training_frequency_matched_items(recent_positions,
                                                     exclude=history)
        recent_context = replace_in_place(context, recent_positions, substitutes)
        random_context = replace_in_place(context, random_positions, substitutes)
        cache paired margins, target ranks, HR@10, and subset overlap
aggregate draws within user
bootstrap users within each category; report paired recent-minus-random differences
return metrics and metric_definitions
finally restore RNG states and model mode

originality.positive: Combines anchor preservation, coupled substitutions, and matched position controls within the existing HSTU diagnostic contract.
originality.negative: Input corruption and matched controls are established techniques; this is an application-specific protocol rather than a new model class.

future_potential.positive: Provides an inexpensive foundation for testing whether diagnostic signals prospectively predict successful single-model HSTU changes.
future_potential.negative: Replacement sensitivity may reflect off-distribution corruption and need not predict improved host validation performance.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses existing embedding, feature, scoring, and history interfaces without internal hooks or retraining.
code_difficulty.negative: Frequency matching, coupled corruption draws, padding correctness, and clustered uncertainty require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU mechanisms including pointwise SiLU attention, relative attention biases, and multiplicative gating.
limitations: Does not establish that the supplied implementation exposes every mechanism or that recent-context sensitivity predicts recommendation quality.

related_work.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
contributions: Examines how corruption choices and measurement metrics affect intervention-based localization.
limitations: Its findings do not directly validate recommendation-specific perturbations or interpretations of user intent.

related_work.title: Prakash et al. (2024), negative-sampling study supplied in the research context
contributions: Motivates examining interactions between negative sampling and item-popularity distributions.
limitations: Popularity matching is a diagnostic control and does not guarantee full-catalog evaluation validity.
